title: Conjecture 1.9 (Alon's Conjecture on Ramsey Cayley Graphs)
statement_text: There is a constant $C$ such that every finite group has a $C$-Ramsey Cayley graph.
context_text: Alon [2] conjectured that every finite group of order $N$ has a Cayley graph whose clique number and independence number are both $O(\log N)$. This was verified for cyclic groups by Green [23] using the uniform Cayley graph, but essentially nothing was known in the general case. Over groups such as $\mathbb{F}_{2}^{n}$, the uniform random Cayley graph cannot serve as a witness since its clique number is $\Omega(\log N \log\log N)$ with high probability.
paper_contribution: Proves Alon's conjecture for all abelian groups of order $N$ for almost all $N$; additionally, for finite vector spaces of order $N$ with characteristic $\equiv 1\pmod{4}$, proves the existence of a self-complementary Cayley graph with clique number and independence number both at most $(2+o(1))\log N$.
notes: The conjecture is also listed on the Open Problem Garden [ref 4 in the bibliography].
paper_title: On the clique number of random Cayley graphs and related topics

title: Conjecture 5.1
statement_text: There exists $C>0$ and a two-coloring of $\mathbb{F}_{2}^{n}\setminus\{0\}$ such that there is no subspace $H$ of size $Cn$ for which all nonzero elements of the subspace are monochromatic.
context_text: $\mathbb{F}_2^n$ is the $n$-dimensional vector space over the field with two elements; a subspace $H$ has $2^{\dim H}$ elements, so a subspace of size $Cn$ has dimension about $\log_2(Cn)$. A Cayley graph on a group $G$ with symmetric generating set $S$ has vertex set $G$, with $x\sim y$ iff $xy^{-1}\in S$; a graph on $N$ vertices is $C$-Ramsey if its clique number and independence number are both at most $C\log N$. Alon conjectured that there is a constant $C$ such that every finite group has a $C$-Ramsey Cayley graph. On $\mathbb{F}_2^n$ (with $N=2^n$), if all nonzero elements of a subspace lie in $S$ (resp. outside $S$), that subspace is a clique (resp. an independent set), so a $C$-Ramsey Cayley graph gives a two-coloring of $\mathbb{F}_2^n\setminus\{0\}$ (in $S$ or not) with no monochromatic subspace of size larger than about $Cn$; the conjecture is thus a consequence of Alon's conjecture for $\mathbb{F}_2^n$, proposed as an intermediate step. By the finite unions theorem, every two-coloring of $\mathbb{F}_2^n\setminus\{0\}$ has a monochromatic subspace of any fixed size once $n$ is large, which is why uniform random Cayley graphs on $\mathbb{F}_2^n$ have clique number $\Theta(\log N\log\log N)$. The best lower bound the authors know, adapted from Sanders' bounds for Rado's theorem, is a monochromatic subspace of size a bounded number of iterated logarithms of $n$, so the true bound may be much smaller than $Cn$. The authors prove Alon's conjecture for abelian groups of order $N$ for almost all $N$ (including $\mathbb{F}_p^n$ for $p\ge5$), but it remains wide open for $\mathbb{F}_2^n$ and $\mathbb{F}_3^n$.
paper_title: On the clique number of random Cayley graphs and related topics
